# TabForge AI — LLM Context File
# Use this file to understand the TabForge AI library API when helping developers write code.
# GitHub: https://github.com/tabforgeai/tabforge-ai
# Maven: io.github.tabforgeai:tabforge-ai:3.0.0

## What is TabForge AI?

A Jakarta EE library with two independent modules:
- **EasyAI** — add AI assistants, chatbots, RAG, autonomous agents, persistent vector store (Milvus), structured extraction, live event streaming, and ambient activity memory to Jakarta EE apps
- **DynTabs** — multi-tab PrimeFaces UI with a custom CDI scope per tab (@TabScoped)

Target runtime: Jakarta EE (CDI, EJB, GlassFish, WildFly, Payara). Also works in plain Java (no container needed).

---

## SETUP

### Maven dependency
```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>io.github.tabforgeai</groupId>
    <artifactId>tabforge-ai</artifactId>
    <version>3.0.0</version>
</dependency>
```

### Configuration — src/main/resources/easyai.properties
```properties
easyai.provider=openai
easyai.api-key=sk-YOUR-KEY
easyai.model-name=gpt-4o-mini
```

Supported providers: `openai`, `ollama`

For Ollama (local, free):
```properties
easyai.provider=ollama
easyai.model-name=llama3
```

**IMPORTANT:** Add `-parameters` compiler flag to maven-compiler-plugin — required for correct method parameter name discovery by EasyAI.
```xml
<plugin>
    <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
    <configuration>
        <compilerArgs><arg>-parameters</arg></compilerArgs>
    </configuration>
</plugin>
```

---

## EASYAI API

### 1. Simple Chat — EasyAI.chat()

```java
// Minimal
Conversation chat = EasyAI.chat().build();
String answer = chat.send("What is a HashMap?");

// With memory and system message
Conversation chat = EasyAI.chat()
    .withMemory(20)
    .withSystemMessage("You are a helpful Java tutor.")
    .build();

// Override provider per conversation
Conversation chat = EasyAI.chat()
    .withProvider("ollama")
    .withModel("llama3")
    .withTemperature(0.3)
    .withMaxTokens(500)
    .build();
```

### 2. AI Assistant — EasyAI.assistant()

Define an interface, EasyAI creates an AI implementation at runtime.

```java
@EasyAIAssistant(systemMessage = "You are a helpful code reviewer")
public interface CodeReviewer {
    String review(String code);
}

CodeReviewer reviewer = EasyAI.assistant(CodeReviewer.class).build();
String feedback = reviewer.review("public void foo() { ... }");
```

### 3. Assistant with Tools (AI calls your Java methods)

**Tools are opt-in (since 3.0.0): only methods you mark with `@EasyTool` are callable.**
Everything else on the service stays invisible to the model — so a prompt-injected
model can't reach destructive methods like `cancelOrder`/`deleteUser`. Works on POJOs
and injected EJB proxies alike.

```java
// Your service — annotate the methods you want the AI to be able to call
public class OrderService {
    @EasyTool("Finds an order by its ID")
    public String findOrder(String orderId) { ... }

    @EasyTool("Cancels an active order. Only works for unshipped orders.")
    public String cancelOrder(String orderId) { ... }

    // NOT annotated -> the model can never see or call this
    public void purgeAllOrders() { ... }
}

@EasyAIAssistant(systemMessage = "You are an e-commerce support bot.")
public interface SupportBot {
    String ask(String question);
}

OrderService orderService = new OrderService();
SupportBot bot = EasyAI.assistant(SupportBot.class)
    .withTools(orderService, userService)   // opt-in: only @EasyTool methods exposed
    .build();

bot.ask("Where is my order #12345?");
// AI automatically calls orderService.findOrder("12345")
```

The `@EasyTool` description is optional (a bare `@EasyTool` uses the method name), but
helps the AI pick the right method. Escape hatch for throwaway prototypes only —
`withAllPublicMethodsAsTools(service)` exposes every public method, annotated or not.

### 4. RAG — Document-Powered AI

Three ways to provide documents:

**A) Static files (classpath or disk):**
```java
@EasyRAG(source = "classpath:company-policy.pdf")
@EasyAIAssistant(systemMessage = "Answer based on company policy.")
public interface PolicyBot {
    String ask(String question);
}

PolicyBot bot = EasyAI.assistant(PolicyBot.class).build();
bot.ask("How many vacation days do employees get?");
```

Multiple files: `@EasyRAG(source = {"classpath:doc1.pdf", "classpath:doc2.txt"})`

**B) File path at runtime:**
```java
PolicyBot bot = EasyAI.assistant(PolicyBot.class)
    .withRAG("/path/to/document.pdf")
    .build();
```

**C) byte[] from DMS / database / REST API / user upload:**
```java
byte[] pdfBytes = dmsClient.downloadDocument("DOC-123");

PolicyBot bot = EasyAI.assistant(PolicyBot.class)
    .withRAG(DocumentSource.of("policy.pdf", pdfBytes))
    .build();

// From plain text string:
.withRAG(DocumentSource.ofText("rules", someStringContent))
```

RAG tuning:
```java
@EasyRAG(source = "classpath:manual.pdf", maxResults = 5, minScore = 0.7)
```

**Combine RAG + Tools:**
```java
SalesBot bot = EasyAI.assistant(SalesBot.class)
    .withRAG(DocumentSource.of("catalog.pdf", catalogBytes))
    .withTools(inventoryService, pricingService)
    .build();
```

### 5. EasyAgent — Autonomous Multi-Step Task Execution

The agent autonomously plans and executes sequences of service method calls to complete a complex task. No orchestration code needed.

```java
EasyAgent agent = EasyAI.agent()
    .withServices(inventoryService, paymentService, orderService, shippingService)
    .withMaxSteps(10)               // hard cap on tool calls (strongly recommended)
    .withPlanningPrompt(true)       // instructs LLM to plan before acting
    .withStepListener(step ->
        log.info("Step {}: {}({}) -> {}",
            step.stepNumber(), step.toolName(), step.arguments(), step.result()))
    .build();

String result = agent.execute(
    "Order 2 laptops for user U123, apply loyalty credit, deliver to Belgrade."
);
```

AgentStep record fields: `stepNumber()`, `toolName()`, `arguments()`, `result()`

When step limit is reached, agent returns final answer without further calls.
When a tool throws an exception, result contains: `TOOL_ERROR | tool=X | error=Y | suggestion=...`

**When to use agent vs assistant:**
- Single Q&A with tool calls → `EasyAI.assistant()`
- Multi-step task, conditional branching, autonomous execution → `EasyAI.agent()`

### 6. Persistent RAG with Milvus — EasyAI.indexer() + .withMilvus()

Index documents ONCE into a persistent vector database; assistants query it forever (survives restarts, shared across sessions/server nodes). Use case 4 RAG is in-memory and ephemeral; Milvus is durable and scales to thousands of docs.

```java
// WRITE side — index once (batch job, or on upload):
int n = EasyAI.indexer()
    .toMilvus("localhost", 19530, "company_kb")
    .index("file:/data/policy.pdf", DocumentSource.of("faq.pdf", bytes));

// READ side — any assistant queries the same store, instantly:
KbBot bot = EasyAI.assistant(KbBot.class)
    .withMilvus("localhost", 19530, "company_kb")
    .build();
bot.ask("How many vacation days do employees get?");
```

`.withMilvus(...)` takes precedence over `.withRAG(...)` / `@EasyRAG`. Connection can come from `easyai.milvus.*` properties via no-arg `.toMilvus()` / `.withMilvus()`. The dimension (default 384) must match the embedding model. Tuning: `.withMilvus(MilvusConfig.of(...), maxResults, minScore)`.

### 7. Structured Extraction — EasyAI.extract()

Turn unstructured text or a document into a TYPED Java record/POJO — the bridge from AI text into your normal typed-Java world.

```java
record Invoice(String vendor, String invoiceNumber, LocalDate date, BigDecimal total) {}

// From free text:
Invoice inv = EasyAI.extract(Invoice.class).from(emailBody);

// From a document's bytes (parsed by Tika, then extracted, in one call):
Invoice inv = EasyAI.extract(Invoice.class)
    .from(DocumentSource.of("invoice.pdf", pdfBytes));
```

Supports records and POJOs, nested objects, lists, enums, and java.time types. Options:
- `.withRetries(n)` — retry on malformed model JSON (default 2)
- `.validate()` — run Jakarta Bean Validation; throws `ExtractionException` on a violation
- per-call config overrides (`.withModel`, `.withApiKey`, ...); extraction defaults to temperature 0.0

### 8. Live Event Stream — observe the AI as it works

Get a live callback for each step the AI takes (tool call, result, agent start/finish), e.g. to drive a real-time UI activity panel. The library stays transport-agnostic — you decide where events go (SSE, WebSocket, log).

```java
EasyAgent agent = EasyAI.agent()
    .withServices(orderService, paymentService)
    .withEventListener(event -> activityBridge.onEvent(event))   // EasyAIEvent per step
    .build();
```

Available on `chat()`, `assistant()`, and `agent()` via `.withEventListener(...)`. The agent additionally offers `.withStepListener(step -> ...)` for a typed `AgentStep` (stepNumber/toolName/arguments/result).

### 9. Ambient Activity Memory — .withActivityContext()

The assistant resolves "this"/"that" from what the user JUST DID in the UI, with no typed context. Mirror image of the live event stream: UI → AI instead of AI → UI.

```java
// 1. Capture (opt-in). Navigation:
@DynTab(name = "OrdersDynTab", uniqueIdentifier = "Orders", trackActivity = true)
public class OrdersBean extends BaseDyntabCdiBean { ... }   // records tab open/select

//    ...and/or business actions:
@ActivityTracked(type = Type.BUSINESS_ACTION, verb = "view",
                 entityType = "order", entityIdParams = "orderId")
public String viewOrder(String orderId) { ... }            // records "viewed order ORD-002"

// 2. Inject the recent activity into the assistant (re-read fresh on every call):
@Inject ActivityStore activityStore;

ActivityContext ctx = ActivityContext.of(activityStore)
    .forSession(sessionId).forTab(tabId).build();    // omit forTab() for app-wide scope

OrdersAssistant bot = EasyAI.assistant(OrdersAssistant.class)
    .withTools(orderService)         // so it can ACT on "this"
    .withActivityContext(ctx)        // so it KNOWS what "this" is
    .build();

bot.ask("cancel this");              // resolves to the order just viewed
```

- `forSession(s).forTab(t)` → per-tab deixis ("cancel this order"). Omit `forTab` → session-wide orientation ("what tab am I on?").
- In-memory, per-session, ephemeral by default (`ActivityStore` SPI, `InMemoryActivityStore` default). Also `.window(Duration)`, `.limit(n)`, `.renderer(...)`.
- Capture is opt-in: nothing is recorded without `@DynTab(trackActivity=true)` or `@ActivityTracked`.

---

## JAKARTA EE / CDI INTEGRATION

### @Inject assistant (no tools)
```java
@EasyAIAssistant(systemMessage = "You are a helpful Java tutor")
public interface JavaTutor {
    String ask(String question);
}

@Inject JavaTutor tutor;  // CDI extension creates @ApplicationScoped instance automatically
```

### @Inject assistant with auto-wired tools
```java
@EasyAIAssistant(
    systemMessage = "You are an e-commerce support bot",
    tools = {OrderService.class, InventoryService.class}
)
public interface SupportBot {
    String ask(String question);
}

@Inject SupportBot bot;  // OrderService and InventoryService resolved from CDI container
```

### EJB beans as tools
Mark callable methods with @EasyTool; pass @Stateless, @Stateful, @Singleton EJBs directly — transactions, security, interceptors preserved. Opt-in applies to EJBs too.
```java
@Inject OrderService orderService;  // EJB proxy; its @EasyTool methods are the tools

SupportBot bot = EasyAI.assistant(SupportBot.class)
    .withTools(orderService)        // EJB proxy detected automatically; only @EasyTool methods exposed
    .build();
```

### EasyAgent in CDI — use @PostConstruct
```java
@Named @ApplicationScoped
public class AgentBean {

    @Inject OrderService orderService;
    @Inject PaymentService paymentService;

    private EasyAgent agent;

    @PostConstruct
    public void init() {
        // IMPORTANT: build agent here, not at field initialization
        // @Inject fields are not yet populated at field init time
        agent = EasyAI.agent()
            .withServices(orderService, paymentService)
            .withMaxSteps(10)
            .build();
    }

    public String process(String task) {
        return agent.execute(task);
    }
}
```

---

## ANNOTATIONS REFERENCE

| Annotation | Where | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `@EasyAIAssistant` | interface | Marks as AI assistant; `systemMessage` sets personality |
| `@EasyTool` | method | **Opt-in gate (required to expose a method as a tool).** `value` (optional) describes it to help the AI pick the right method. Escape hatch: `withAllPublicMethodsAsTools()`/`withAllPublicMethodsAsServices()` |
| `@EasyRAG` | interface | Loads documents for RAG; `source`, `maxResults`, `minScore` |
| `@ActivityTracked` | method | Records a user-activity event when called; `type`, `verb`, `entityType`, `entityIdParams`, `includeText`. Read back via `.withActivityContext(...)` |

---

## CONFIGURATION REFERENCE

| Property | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `easyai.provider` | `openai` or `ollama` | `openai` |
| `easyai.api-key` | API key | (none) |
| `easyai.model-name` | Model name | (provider default) |
| `easyai.base-url` | Custom endpoint | (provider default) |
| `easyai.temperature` | 0.0–1.0 | (provider default) |
| `easyai.max-tokens` | Max response length | (provider default) |
| `easyai.milvus.host` | Milvus host (use case 6) | `localhost` |
| `easyai.milvus.port` | Milvus port | `19530` |
| `easyai.milvus.collection` | Collection name | (required) |
| `easyai.milvus.dimension` | Embedding dimension | `384` |

Programmatic override:
```java
EasyAI.configure(EasyAIConfig.builder()
    .provider("openai")
    .apiKey("sk-...")
    .modelName("gpt-4o")
    .temperature(0.7)
    .build());
```

---

## ERROR HANDLING

```java
try {
    return bot.ask(userQuestion);
} catch (Exception e) {
    return "Error: " + EasyAI.extractErrorMessage(e);
}
```

`EasyAI.extractErrorMessage(e)` parses JSON error responses from OpenAI-compatible providers.

LangChain4J exceptions: `AuthenticationException`, `RateLimitException`, `InvalidRequestException`, `InternalServerException`

---

## COMMON MISTAKES

- **Missing `-parameters` compiler flag** → method parameters appear as `arg0`, `arg1` instead of real names. AI cannot understand what to pass to methods.
- **Building EasyAgent at field initialization in CDI** → NullPointerException because `@Inject` fields aren't populated yet. Always build in `@PostConstruct`.
- **Tool methods returning complex objects** → AI works best with String return values. Ensure `toString()` is meaningful, or convert to String in the method.
- **No `withMaxSteps()`** → agent may make many sequential calls, increasing token cost significantly.
- **Model name with quotes in properties file** → `easyai.model-name="gpt-4o"` fails. Use `easyai.model-name=gpt-4o` (no quotes).

---

## DYNTABS — Multi-Tab PrimeFaces UI

### Define a tab bean
```java
@Named
@TabScoped
@DynTab(name = "OrdersDynTab", title = "Orders", includePage = "/WEB-INF/include/orders/orders.xhtml")
public class OrdersBean extends BaseDyntabCdiBean {

    @Inject OrderService orderService;

    @Override
    protected void accessPointMethod(Map parameters) {
        // called when tab opens — load data here
        orders = orderService.findAll();
    }

    @Override
    protected void exitPointMethod() {
        // called when tab closes — cleanup here
    }
}
```

### Open a tab from a menu item
```xml
<p:menuitem value="Orders" action="uishell:Orders"/>
```

### Key DynTabs features
- `@TabScoped` — one CDI bean instance per open tab (independent instances)
- `sendMessageToAllAppModules(payload)` / `onApplicationMessage()` — inter-tab messaging
- `closeAndReturnValueToCaller(value)` — child tab returns value to parent
- `@DynTab(securedResource=true, allowedRoles={"ADMIN"})` — declarative security
- `@DynTab(trackActivity=true)` — records tab open/select onto the ambient activity timeline (feeds EasyAI Ambient Activity Memory, use case 9)
- Open tabs programmatically with parameters at runtime
